Subject: Mapping sprint & technical readiness for pilot

Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo today. We liked the latency and the routing options. Samir and I started sketching an evaluation plan but wanted to reuse any MAP/canvas templates you typically share with customers so we can align stakeholders quickly.

Two asks to start:
- Can you share a concise MAP template (roles, milestones, success criteria) and a short technical readiness checklist we can run against our infra team?
- We are targeting a 30-day trial starting mid-April; what does a common close/acceptance timeline look like from your experience?

If possible, can we schedule a 60–90 min workshop next week to walk through the MAP and confirm owners? Samir is the infra lead (CC'd).

Thanks —
Elena

Subject: Re: Mapping sprint & technical readiness for pilot

Elena —

Great to connect today. Attaching a compact starter set that we use for most pilot MAPs: a one-page sprint canvas (MAP_Sprint_Canvas_v1.gdoc), a technical readiness checklist tailored to on-prem/VPC pilots (Pilot_Technical_Readiness_Checklist.pdf), and a 30–60 minute Week0 slide set we run in the kickoff (Week0_Workshop_Slides.gslides). Links below as well.

Quick highlights and suggested next steps:
- Ownership: Prod/Infra owner (you), Security/Compliance (internal reviewer), Product/PM (business objectives), CSM (Marissa) and AE (Ben) to coordinate timelines.
- Milestones (recommended):
  * Week0: Kickoff + technical runway validation (SSO, network, KMS access)
  * Week1–2: Integration + baseline eval (latency/cost, small traffic)
  * Week3–4: Feature validation + acceptance testing (business prompts/evals)
  * Post-pilot: Close decision and rollout plan (30–90 day prod ramp)
- Acceptance criteria (example):
  * Avg generation latency < 600ms for p95 on target requests
  * Correctness score on evaluation prompts >= 85% (agreed prompt set)
  * No data exfiltration issues; audit logs enabled

Can you confirm:
1) Which region your pilot infra will run in (us-east1 / us-west1 / eu-west1)?
2) Does NovaSanity use SSO + SCIM today for vendor tools, and who is our infra contact for KMS / firewall rules?

Propose workshop slots: Apr 12 10am–11:30am PT, Apr 13 9am–10:30am PT. I can send a calendar invite with the Week0 slides and a short pre-read.

Links/attachments:
- MAP starter doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcdMockedLinkMAP
- Week0 slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1SlideMockedLink

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt

- We do have SSO + SCIM (Okta) for vendor tools; KMS is managed in GCP (key admin is Samir).
- For data retention and audit logs: we need the pilot to document retention windows and log export options for compliance. Can you point us to where that gets captured in the MAP or slides?

Elena
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mapping sprint & technical readiness for pilot

Thanks Elena —

On behalf of the team, quick answers and a proposed evaluation cadence you can copy into the MAP: 

- Data retention / audit logs: We capture retention windows and log export responsibilities in the technical readiness checklist (see attached PDF). During Week0 we walk the export path (Cloud Audit Logs -> SIEM) and note retention targets; I’ll add a short table to the MAP doc with fields: retention window, export destination, owner.

Proposed evaluation plan (copyable into the MAP):
Phase A — Week0 (Kickoff + Tech Validation)
  - Objectives: Validate network connectivity, KMS access, SSO/SCIM sync, and baseline perf test
  - Deliverables: Completed checklist, workshop notes, test token for eval traffic

Phase B — Week1–2 (Integration + Baseline Eval)
  - Objectives: Route a subset of production-like traffic, collect latency/cost baseline, run prompt set (50 prompts)
  - Success criteria: p95 latency < 600ms, cost per 1k tokens within target band, correctness >= 80%

Phase C — Week3–4 (Acceptance + Decision)
  - Objectives: Run acceptance prompt set (200 prompts), validate failover + fallback policies, finalize rollout plan
  - Decision: Sign-off + proposed reserved capacity date

Next steps from our side:
- Hannah will send the workshop invite for Apr 12 10–11:30am PT (Week0 agenda + slides).
- Samir: if you can confirm KMS and a firewall contact before the workshop, we’ll assign the prework checklist items.
- Marissa: I’ll sync on customer success handoffs and draft the 30-day production ramp options to present at acceptance.

Looking forward —
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference.com
